# Review capacity under delayed availability of withdrawal information

A lag in the availability of administrative status can change whether a case is actionable when staff allocate review slots. On the existing day-60 OULAD 2014J roster, use the two original all-registration scores with no refitting. Compare a register current at day 60, stale by 1, 7, 14 or 30 days, and an unfiltered register. For a lag L remove only known exits on or before day 60−L. Use final recorded Withdrawn and actual eligibility at day 60 for retrospective scoring. The same-day status rule is the ideal administrative reference. Apply a uniform delay to dates as a counterfactual; the release has no reporting latency measure.

Set each module's capacity to floor(10% of its true eligible roster) in every scenario. Evaluate 5% and 20% as sensitivity checks. This is a fixed exogenous allocation for the comparison; a system with stale status cannot infer exact current enrollment unaided. Use equal probability within a score tie crossing the budget. Report expected stale seats, captures among still-eligible subsequent withdrawals, and actionable precision over the entire fixed budget. Include a uniform-random within-module selection control for each status policy. Verify that total seats remain fixed, that stale seats cannot decrease as status delay increases for a fixed ranking and that recovered eligible cases never exceed the number of seats freed. Condition estimates on this archived roster and fixed predictions. The study reuses a previously examined presentation and does not measure the benefit of contacting a student.
